moduleTitle: Executing tests across multiple browsers in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain why local runs are limited to Chrome and what mechanism removes that limitation.
Configure a cross-browser run across Testim's grid, a Selenium grid, or via the CLI/Scheduler.

elements.description: When running locally — from the editor or the Test List — tests can only run on Chrome. This is a hard constraint of local execution, not a configurable setting.

Use CLI/Scheduler with supported browser/OS configurations for a cross-browser matrix. The editor also supports a single grid test. Supported combinations depend on the grid; selecting desktop browser configurations is not evidence of physical-device or native-mobile coverage.

--grid selects the configured grid by name. --test-config selects browser/OS/resolution or other test configuration overrides; these flags have different roles. Verify both target infrastructure and the supported browser configuration.

bulletPoints: Local web playback uses Chrome; a single editor remote grid run is separate.
CLI/Scheduler support configured matrices on compatible grids.
--grid selects the grid; --test-config selects the test configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting the editor Play button to cover cross-browser coverage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a passing local editor run means the test also works on Firefox, Safari, and Edge.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A local run only ever exercises Chrome. Cross-browser confidence requires an actual CLI or Scheduler run against a grid configured for the other browsers.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which browser(s) can a locally run test (editor or Test List) execute on?

options.text: Any installed browser, selected per run.
Whatever browser was used when recording.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is a hard constraint, not a setting.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented local web playback workflow uses Chrome. A single remote editor grid run is separate; CLI/Scheduler provide configured matrix execution.

optionExplanations.A: The documented local web playback uses Chrome.
optionExplanations.B: It does not choose any installed browser for that local workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Firefox is not this local playback browser.
optionExplanations.D: Recording browser does not determine local playback.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which documented workflow runs a configured matrix of supported Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge targets?

options.text: Nothing extra — local runs already cover all four browsers.
Using the CLI or Scheduler, targeting Testim's grid or a compatible Selenium grid.
Manually installing each browser on the Testim servers.
Re-recording the test separately in each browser.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's not about re-recording, it's about the execution mechanism.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CLI/Scheduler use supported grid and test configurations for the matrix. Available OS/browser combinations depend on the grid; this does not certify physical mobile-device coverage.

optionExplanations.A: A local run does not establish every browser target.
optionExplanations.B: CLI/Scheduler support a configured grid matrix.
optionExplanations.C: Manually installing browsers on managed servers is not the documented matrix workflow.
optionExplanations.D: Separate recording per browser is not required by this workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which CLI option is used to specify the grid a run should target?
practiceQuiz.hint: Grid selection and test-configuration selection are separate CLI flags.
practiceQuiz.rationale: --grid names the grid. --test-config selects browser/OS/resolution configuration, --branch selects a branch and --parallel sets concurrency.

optionExplanations.A: Timeout retry control does not select the grid.
optionExplanations.B: Branch selection does not name a grid.
optionExplanations.C: --grid selects the configured grid by name.
optionExplanations.D: Parallel count does not name the grid.

quickRecap.value: Chrome only — a hard constraint, not a setting.
Use CLI/Scheduler configurations for a supported grid matrix; a single editor grid run is distinct.
Grid name versus test/browser configuration; verify both.
